title: Zanzibar Mix Soup
community: Zanzibar Stone Town — the island's most iconic street food
author: Chef Fatuma

heritage.origin: Zanzibar Stone Town — the most complex street food in East Africa
heritage.history: Urojo is Zanzibar's most complex and celebrated street food — a sour, tangy soup made from a mango-coconut broth, served with a bewildering array of toppings: bhajias, mishkaki, kachori, cassava chips, boiled eggs, and a drizzle of peanut-chilli sauce. It is the food that defines Zanzibar's Stone Town evenings — eaten standing at the Forodhani Gardens as the sun sets over the Indian Ocean. No two vendors' urojo is identical; each guards their recipe fiercely.

desc: Tanzanian Urojo — Zanzibar's legendary 'mix' soup. A tangy, slightly sour mango and coconut broth thickened with chickpea flour, topped with bhajias, mishkaki, kachori, cassava chips, and a peanut-chilli drizzle. The most complex, most celebrated street food in East Africa.
longDesc: Urojo is impossible to describe to someone who has never eaten it — it is simultaneously a soup, a salad, a snack, and a complete meal. The broth is tangy from green mango and tamarind, slightly sour, deeply spiced, and thickened to a soup consistency. The toppings are applied individually by the vendor: bhajias for crunch, mishkaki for protein, kachori for substance, cassava chips for starch. The final drizzle of peanut sauce and pili pili ties everything together. Eating urojo at Forodhani Gardens as the sun sets over the Indian Ocean is one of East Africa's great food experiences.
steps: Make broth: combine water, grated mango, tamarind, and spices. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk chickpea flour with ½ cup cold water until smooth. Pour into simmering broth, stirring constantly.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 15—20 minutes, stirring regularly, until thickened to a thin soup consistency.
Adjust tartness with tamarind and salt.
Make peanut sauce: whisk peanut butter with pili pili, lemon, and water until smooth.
To serve: ladle hot broth into a bowl. Add bhajia, mishkaki piece, kachori, cassava chips, egg half.
Add extra pili pili to taste.
chefTips: The broth tartness is the soul of urojo — adjust tamarind until it is distinctly sour.
Every topping must be hot when assembled — cold toppings sink and make the broth lukewarm.
The chickpea flour must be stirred in slowly and continuously to prevent lumps.
Urojo is always assembled to order — never pre-assembled.
commonMistakes: Insufficient tartness — urojo must be sour.
Lumpy broth — stir the chickpea flour continuously.
cookingScience: Chickpea flour (besan) contains significantly more protein and starch than wheat flour — when cooked in liquid, the starch gelatinises and the proteins denature, creating a smooth thickening effect. The tart green mango and tamarind provide tartaric and citric acids that create urojo's characteristic sour profile.
sustainabilityTips: Urojo uses green mango — the unripe fruit that would otherwise be discarded from the harvest.
storage: Broth keeps 2 days refrigerated. Toppings prepared fresh.
healthBenefits: Complete meal — protein, carbohydrate, and vegetables.
culturalNote: Urojo is Zanzibar's most complex and most beloved street food — the dish that captures the entire history of the Indian Ocean trade in a single bowl. The sour mango broth (African), the coconut milk (coastal), the bhajia (Indian), the mishkaki (Swahili), the peanut sauce (mainland) — all of Zanzibar's food cultures in one bowl.
